projects.title: MIRSAD
projects.description: Shared memory for AI agents: bi-temporal facts, first-class decision units, and conflicts that stay pending until the owner rules.

case.problem: AI assistants like Claude and ChatGPT each start with amnesia: nothing one of them learns survives into the next session, and when two agents record different versions of a fact there is no trace of who decided what, or why.
case.solution: A shared memory hub with bi-temporal facts (every value keeps its validity window), first-class Decision units that store reasons, evidence and rejected alternatives, and a conflict queue where a challenged fact stays pending until the owner rules. Ships as an MCP server (13 tools) with a live graph viewer and a PyPI package; also deployed on Cloudflare Workers + D1.
case.role: Designed and built solo — core engine, MCP server, viewer, deployment and the release process.

lines: # MIRSAD
IMG0
### Shared memory for AI agents: bi-temporal facts, first-class decision units, and conflicts that stay pending until the owner rules.
Mirsad gives AI agents a shared, living memory. Facts are stored
bi-temporally in SQLite with episodes as provenance, and disagreements
between agents become Decision units — the system never judges; the owner
has the final word. It ships as the mirsad-mcp package on PyPI and runs live
on Cloudflare Workers + D1, with Claude and ChatGPT connected.
Built with Python · MCP · SQLite · Cloudflare D1
[Visit](https://github.com/amkkoussay/Mersad)

projects.title: Rain2Risk
projects.description: Relative flood-risk screening with a transparent weighted model — built for screening, not prediction.

case.problem: Flood risk in Tunis is published as static maps and reports; a resident cannot ask 'what about my street?' and get an answer they can check.
case.solution: Five weighted factors — rainfall 40%, slope 20%, elevation 15%, built-up share 15%, distance to water 10% — computed per map cell from OpenWeather rainfall and Open-Meteo terrain, exactly as documented in the README. The ESA WorldCover land-cover layer is currently unavailable in production and is shown as unavailable, never guessed.
case.role: Solo build — scoring backend, methodology write-up and the Leaflet map frontend.

lines: # Rain2Risk
IMG0
### Relative flood-risk screening with a transparent weighted model — built for screening, not prediction.
rain2risk turns rainfall and terrain signals into a relative flood-risk
picture using a published weighted model (40/20/15/15/10). The methodology
is stated openly in the README, including what the tool does not claim: it
screens relative risk, it does not predict floods.
Built with Python · Leaflet · OpenWeather · Open-Meteo · ESA WorldCover
[Visit](https://rain2risk.vercel.app)

projects.title: CropGuide
projects.description: Plant-disease guidance backed by a source-verified knowledge base: 18 crops, 184 verified disease records.

case.problem: Plant apps look at one photo and announce a disease with confidence — a guess dressed as a diagnosis, which can push a farmer toward the wrong treatment.
case.solution: Crop-first triage: Plant.id suggests the crop, Gemini Vision extracts only the symptom codes actually visible in the photo, and matches are checked against a knowledge base of 18 crops and 184 source-verified disease records. When the evidence is too thin, the app abstains instead of guessing.
case.role: Solo build — curated the verified knowledge base record by record and built the app around the abstention rule.

lines: # CropGuide
IMG0
### Plant-disease guidance backed by a source-verified knowledge base: 18 crops, 184 verified disease records.
CropGuide identifies possible plant diseases from a photo. Its knowledge
base was rebuilt from real, source-backed records only — templated or
generated records were rejected. Every one of the 184 records across 18
crops is traceable to its source.
Built with JavaScript · Plant.id · Gemini Vision · SQLite

projects.title: Clinique
projects.description: Clinic management platform with a role-aware AI assistant, an integration API, and automated appointment emails.

case.problem: A small clinic runs patients, appointments and records across paper files and chat threads; nothing is searchable and reminders depend on memory.
case.solution: A clinic management platform: patients, appointments, medical records and billing with role-based access (admin, doctor, receptionist, patient), a FHIR-shaped REST API, an AI assistant whose tools are scoped to the caller's role, and n8n webhooks that fire booking confirmations and cancellations.
case.role: Solo build — Flask/SQLite platform, role-scoped chatbot tools and the n8n event integration, tested end-to-end live.

projects.title: AI Health Assistant
projects.description: Full-stack health informatics and symptom-analysis application. Exploratory project.

case.problem: Symptom checkers rush to name a disease; for an Arabic speaker the options are worse — translated lists with no sense of urgency or safety.
case.solution: An Arabic-first health explainer (Nabd) that organizes what the user feels, explains what it may mean and what step comes next, puts safety signals first, and never claims a diagnosis.
case.role: Solo build — exploratory project; content structure and the safety-first interaction.

projects.title: Mapping Equity GeoAI
projects.description: Geospatial exploration of how services and risk are distributed across places. Exploratory project.

case.problem: Unequal access to public services is easy to assert and hard to show; without spatial evidence it stays an opinion.
case.solution: A geospatial analysis of service coverage shipped as a full documentation package — evidence register, methodology, data lineage and a validation report — so every claim in it can be re-checked.
case.role: Solo research and build — exploratory / proof of concept.

projects.title: BakeryERP (Pann)
projects.description: A modular Flask application with a layered database and service architecture. Proof of concept.

case.problem: A small bakery tracks stock, purchasing and profit in notebooks; reordering is guesswork and losses surface weeks late.
case.solution: BakeryERP: inventory and purchasing with predictive reorder suggestions, profitability analytics, PDF/Excel exports and role-based access (admin, manager, cashier, customer); demo accounts are only ever seeded with explicit passwords, never defaults.
case.role: Solo build — Flask ERP with database migrations and a test suite.

projects.title: BakeryERP Pro
projects.description: Bakery operations suite: point of sale, inventory, production, purchasing and online orders in one system.

case.problem: A bakery runs sales, stock and production on paper and scattered sheets; nothing connects what was sold to what must be baked or bought.
case.solution: One operations system: point of sale, inventory driven by bills of materials, production and purchasing orders, online orders, and reports for profitability, waste and inventory prediction.
case.role: Solo design and build — Flask blueprints, service/repository modules, SQL schema and migrations.
